transcript.text: hoover washer drier showing EO3 wont drain, ive done the filter its clean. H3DS4965DACE. pump just buzzes. do i need a new pump??

A pump that buzzes but does not drain, with a clean filter, is most often either something jammed in the impeller/pump or a failed pump; a kinked or blocked drain hose can give the same result. Switch it off and unplug it, put towels and a shallow tray down, remove the filter, then use a torch to look through the opening and gently turn the small plastic impeller with a finger. If it is jammed or the vanes are damaged, the drain pump is the likely faulty component; if it turns freely, check the drain hose and its waste connection next before condemning the pump.

done that with power off. impeller spins totally freely, no resistance at all, feels like its not connected to anything. torch shows one fin looks snapped. drain hose is clear too, disconnected and checked

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump (jammed or failed)]
Yes — on that evidence the drain pump is the likely failed part. A buzzing pump with a clear filter and drain hose, plus an impeller that spins freely with a snapped vane and feels disconnected, points to damage inside the pump rather than a remaining blockage. EO3 is consistent with a drain fault, although I cannot confirm that code specifically for this exact model. The pump will need replacing; it is not normally repairable internally. I could not confirm an exact parts match for H3DS4965DACE, so use the full model and product/serial number from the rating plate when checking Hoover spares, or book an appliance engineer to supply and fit it. Keep the machine unplugged and avoid running further cycles until it is repaired, as it will not be able to empty properly.
